deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (previous page). Gauss defines two even entire power series P(φ), Q(φ) with P(0)=Q(0)=1. They satisfy
(log P)'' = -Q^2/P^2, i.e. PP'' - P'^2 + Q^2 = 0, and (log Q)'' = -μ^2 P^2/Q^2.
The quotient s = P/Q satisfies ds^2 = dφ^2 (1-s^2)(1-μ^2 s^2). This is the integral ∫ds/sqrt((1-ss)(1-μμss)) written on the previous page. With s(0)=1 this gives s = cd(φ, k=μ), with k the Jacobi modulus. I checked (my verification, not on the page) that P and Q are exactly Weierstrass's Al-functions Al_2 and Al_3, normalized by Al = exp(-k^2 ∫∫ sn^2). Indeed (log dn)'' - k^2 sn^2 = -k^2 cd^2, which is the Q equation. Then cn = P·Al^{-1} and dn = Q·Al^{-1}.

THIS PAGE.

(1) Ansatz lines (top). Put y = log P and z = log Q. Then y'' = -e^{2z-2y} and z'' = -μ^2 e^{2y-2z}. Hence μ^2 e^{4y} y'' = e^{4z} z'' = -μ^2 P^2 Q^2. Gauss writes this as μ e^{4y} ddy = e^{4z} ddz, using 'μ' for μ^2. In functional form: μP^4 ∂(P'/P) = Q^4 ∂(Q'/Q). Likewise ∂(P'/P)·∂(Q'/Q) = μ dφ^2, whose true value is μ^2 dφ^2. He also tests the first-order analogue μ e^{4y}dy = e^{4z}dz, which would give e^{4z} - μ e^{4y} = Const, i.e. Q^4 - μ^2 P^4 = const. Its derivative is the bottom-line expression 'μP^3P' - Q^3Q''. For the test he expands P^4 = 1 - 2φ^2 + (1/6)(10+2μ^2)φ^4 and Q^4 = 1 - 2μ^2φ^2 + (1/6)(2μ^2+10μ^4)φ^4.

(2) Difference series. (Q-P)/(1-μ^2) = φ^2/2 - (1+μ^2)φ^4/24 + (1-μ^2+μ^4)φ^6/720 - (1+μ^2)(1-20μ^2+μ^4)φ^8/40320.
The φ^8 term is found by dividing 1-20t+0t^2+20t^3-t^4 (t=μ^2) by 1-t, giving 1-19t-19t^2+t^3 (the scratch '1-19-19+1'). This factors as (1+t)(1-20t+t^2).

(3) Squares. (Q^2-P^2)/(1-μ^2) = φ^2 - (1+μ^2)φ^4/3 + (4+11μ^2+4μ^4)φ^6/90.
Its square root is the odd function R = φ - (1+μ^2)φ^3/6 + (1+4μ^2+μ^4)φ^5/120 + ...
This R equals Q·sd = P·sc = Weierstrass Al_1, and Q^2 - P^2 = k'^2 R^2 is dn^2 - cn^2 = k'^2 sn^2. A partly struck line 1 - ½(1+μ^2)φ^2 + (1/24)(1+4μ^2+μ^4)φ^4 - (1/720)(1+μ^2)(1+13μ^2+μ^4)φ^6 is most plausibly R'(φ).

(4) Main result: the series to φ^12.
P = 1 - φ^2/2 + (1+2t)φ^4/4! - (1+6t+8t^2)φ^6/6! + (1+12t+60t^2+32t^3)φ^8/8! - (1+20t+348t^2+448t^3+128t^4)φ^10/10! + (1+30t+2372t^2+4600t^3+2880t^4+512t^5)φ^12/12!
Q = 1 - tφ^2/2 + (2t+t^2)φ^4/4! - (8t+6t^2+t^3)φ^6/6! + (32t+60t^2+12t^3+t^4)φ^8/8! - (128t+...)φ^10/10!
The Q coefficients are the P coefficients reversed. This is Q(φ;μ) = P(μφ;1/μ), the reciprocal-modulus symmetry Al_3(u,k) = Al_2(ku,1/k).

Method (scratch tables). He writes A_n for (2n)! times the coefficient. He substitutes into PP'' - P'^2 + Q^2 = 0, so the products give binomial convolutions. These are the rows 1,12,66,220,495,792,924 = C(12,k); 4·C(10,k) = 4,40,180,480,840,1008; C(10,k); and 4·C(8,k). He then sums column by column; the table's last row is 1, 30, 2372, 4600, 2880, 512.
Control check at μ=1, where P = Q = e^{-φ^2/2}: the coefficient polynomial must sum to (2n-1)!!. Indeed 945 = 1+20+348+448+128 and 10395 = 1+30+2372+4600+2880+512. The marginal '945, 10395, 2880 x y 512, 6972-x-y' uses this to fix the unknown middle coefficients.

(5) Factoring attempt. He tries to split 1+44t+120t^2+44t^3+t^4 as (1+pt+t^2)(1+qt+t^2), so p+q = 44 and pq = 118. Then (p-q)^2 = 1936 - 472 = 1464, which is not a square, so no rational factorization.

Other scratch. Rows 1.8.26.40.15.-48.-84, 1.14.84.152.64 and the (1)^2(2)... notation are uninterpretable without more context. Words such as 'Lat', 'Pers', 'Pryt', 'Credite', 'ih Iddek' and 'gränzfo..' are pen trials.
errors: The ansatz μe^{4y}dy = e^{4z}dz ⇒ e^{4z} - μe^{4y} = Const (Q^4 - μ^2P^4 = const) is false. Only the second-derivative relation μ^2P^4(log P)'' = Q^4(log Q)'' holds. With Gauss's own P^4, Q^4 the φ^4 term of Q^4 - μ^2P^4 is -(4/3)μ^2(1-μ^2) ≠ 0. He appears to have been testing this and did not use it.
'μ' is used where μ^2 is meant in μP^4∂(P'/P) = Q^4∂(Q'/Q) and ∂(P'/P)∂(Q'/Q) = μdφ^2. This is a notational slip, not a conceptual one.
The square-root series line reads +(1/60)(1+4μμ+μ^4). The correct coefficient of sqrt((Q^2-P^2)/(1-μ^2)) is (1+4μ^2+μ^4)/120. This is either a slip or a misreading.

The partly struck line with -(1/720)(1+μ^2)(1+13μ^2+μ^4)φ^6 does not match the derivative of R. R's φ^7 coefficient is -(1+μ^2)(1+8μ^2+μ^4)/5040, so R' should have (1+8μ^2+μ^4). At μ=1, R = e^{-φ^2/2}sinh φ gives -20/5040, not -30/5040. The line may refer to something else.
In the Q series the φ^10 denominator is written 362880 (=9!). It should be 3628800 (=10!), as in the P series.

The φ^12 term of P has an empty denominator (should be 12! = 479001600), a '?' and a struck μ^4 coefficient. The final value 2372 is consistent with the (2n-1)!! check but is not independently verified here.

results.what: Entire functions P, Q (and R) with P/Q = cd(φ,μ), R/Q = sd(φ,μ), defined by (log P)'' = -Q^2/P^2, (log Q)'' = -μ^2P^2/Q^2. Power series computed to φ^12 with polynomial coefficients in μ^2.
results.modern_name: Weierstrass Al-functions Al_2, Al_3, Al_1 (theta functions in power-series form, normalized by exp(-k^2∫∫sn^2))
results.usually_credited_to: K. Weierstrass (Al functions, 1840 manuscript, published 1894); Jacobi theta functions (1829)

results.what: Recursive coefficient computation via binomial convolutions from PP''-P'^2+Q^2=0, with the μ=1 check that coefficient sums equal (2n-1)!! because P=e^{-φ^2/2}
results.modern_name: recursive power-series solution of an ODE with a degenerate-modulus check

results.what: Q(φ;μ) = P(μφ;1/μ): coefficient polynomials of Q are reversed P polynomials

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lemniscatic P,Q (sl = P/Q as quotient of entire series) is well known from Werke III, and Schlesinger discussed his anticipation of theta functions. This page extends the idea to general modulus μ, in a form identical to Weierstrass's Al-functions, with explicit coefficients to φ^12. That is a notable concrete detail, though the general fact that Gauss had theta-type functions is known. It is not a new major theorem.

checkable.asserts: Gauss's P and Q series satisfy PP''-P'^2+Q^2=0 through φ^10. Extend Q to φ^12 to test the 2372 coefficient.
QQ''-Q'^2+μ^2P^2=0 (second defining equation), with P, Q as above.
R = Al_1 series. The φ^5 coefficient is /120 (page has /60); the φ^7 coefficient involves 1+8μ^2+μ^4, not 1+13μ^2+μ^4.
Q^4-μ^2P^4 is NOT constant: its φ^4 coefficient is -4*t*(1-t)/3.
No rational factorization into (1+pt+t^2)(1+qt+t^2), since 44^2-4*118=1464 is not a square.
